notes: Cliopatria's 27 Han Dynasty shapes are kept as adjusted or marked wrong (see the counts at the end). ONE STATE OR TWO: the row shares Wikidata Q1068371 with chauhan-dynasty, an Indian Rajput clan; the shared id is an error on Cliopatria's side (the Han page is the Wikipedia title of this row), so this dossier is the Han alone. The Western and Eastern Han and Wang Mang's interregnum are one state in this dossier (a rename in 25, Xin as predecessor and successor), as the colour registry puts the Xin in the Han's colour group; the xin-dynasty dossier is the Xin's own. SHAPES THAT ARE WRONG: (1) the 6 shape (143 km2, 12 cells) is a sliver: 6-8 is the Han with the 36 shape, 9-22 is the Xin. (2) The 224 shape (3,111 of 3,113 cells are Eastern Wu's) cannot be Han: the dynasty ended in the winter of 220 (11 December, List of Han emperors page). (3) Korea: Cliopatria adds the peninsula in 91 (the commanderies fell in 108-107) and drops 108 east-coast cells in 36 (Xuantu left in 75). (4) Yunnan, Guizhou and the Yelang lands are added in 91 (taken 111-109). (5) The Hexi Corridor and Lop Nur are added in 110 (taken 121) and then lost from the 30 shape to 90 for no reason any page gives. (6) The 126 shape hands 350 north-eastern cells to the Xiongnu; no page says so. (7) The 43-50 shape removes the Trung lands that were lost in 40 and regained in 43. (8) The Tarim cells in the 77, 50 and 91 shapes are protectorate (client) land, drawn as a lighter tint by the vassal events with counterpart protectorate-of-the-western-regions; Fergana and Kyrgyzstan cells (162) are taken out. (9) 115-60 BC: the Han and the Xiongnu fought over the oasis states; Cliopatria shows them as Han in 110 (Lop Nur only) and 77 (Shanshan), 50. (10) 197-223: Cliopatria's Han shapes are the nominal realm outside Cao Cao's heartland (197, 207) and then Liu Zhang's and Liu Bei's domain (215), not the land the court governed from Xuchang; replaced on 2026-10-19 by Cao Cao's shapes (see REVISION below).
